title: Choose the visual world for /app/enhance
question: This mobile-first workspace needs to make package fulfillment impossible to miss. Keep the lead direction, choose an alternate, or re-roll.

options.label: The Departure Board
options.thesis: Your package reads as a journey already in motion: every owed photo has a visible status, and one clear gate advances the trip.
options.viewport: On mobile, a compact Pro 1/9 route board sits above the selected portrait; a thumb-level Generate remaining 8 photos gate anchors the screen while candidate stops unfold below.
options.risk: Without generous portrait scale and calm body copy, the system could feel like logistics software rather than a personal photo studio.

raised.raise: Every stage becomes addressable and resumable, with a visible back trail instead of hidden state.
Each screen carries one imperative at full strength; supporting regions stop competing.
Importance is encoded by scale before color: the selected portrait and next action always dominate.
Dense package detail compacts into a phone summary and deploys only when requested.
Motion is reserved for deterministic status changes and remains reversible and readable.

options.label: The Studio Proof Desk
options.lineage: editorial contact sheets and portrait-studio proofing tables
options.thesis: The interface behaves like a photographer presenting proofs: the chosen portrait leads, the contact sheet stays close, and package progress reads like a job ticket.
options.viewport: A large selected proof fills the first mobile fold, with a narrow candidate strip, a handwritten-style best-shot mark, and a clipped fulfillment ticket carrying the single next action.
options.risk: It is the most familiar photography direction and can become intimidating pro-tool cosplay if crop marks and proof notation overpower plain guidance.

options.label: The Calm Instrument Panel
options.thesis: Each package allowance owns one trustworthy instrument while a single central trajectory shows what the user must do next.
options.viewport: The portrait occupies the main instrument glass; candidates, refinements, add-ons, and exports become four separately labeled readings beneath one bright next-action annunciator.
options.case: It matches the lead direction on allowance clarity and state visibility, but professionals identify less naturally with a cockpit than with a photo workflow.
options.risk: The dark technical language can feel specialist, masculine, or high-stakes, making a simple personal task feel harder than it is.

options.label: The HyperCard Stack
options.thesis: Each package stage is one addressable card with a literal back trail and editable choices in place.
options.viewport: A fixed-ratio mobile card shows one task at a time with Back and Continue controls embedded in its border.
options.case: Strong navigation memory, but weak professional-photo identification and insufficient image richness.
options.kept: Addressable, resumable stages with an exact back trail.
options.risk: The retro monochrome treatment would make paid portraits feel like a novelty demo.

options.label: The Profile Poster
options.thesis: Each stage becomes one flat-ink portrait plane and one ranger-voiced imperative.
options.viewport: The selected portrait becomes a four-plane poster above a full-width Generate remaining photos command bar.
options.case: Memorable hierarchy, but the poster language promotes the product more than it helps someone operate it.
options.kept: One imperative per screen with uncompromised flat hierarchy.
options.risk: Generated photos could look falsely color-treated when the interface is too visually entangled with them.

options.label: The Candidate Atlas
options.thesis: Candidates form a ranked field where recommendation strength is visible as magnitude and every package has coordinates.
options.viewport: A bright best-shot anchor centers the candidate field while package coordinates and the next action orbit at quieter scales.
options.case: Ranking can be beautifully legible, but spatial metaphor obscures the straightforward generate-review-export sequence.
options.kept: Encode importance through scale before annotation or color.
options.risk: A constellation of portraits becomes abstract precisely when users need direct comparison.

options.label: The Deployable Sheet
options.thesis: The package opens from a compact summary into linked candidate, refinement, and export regions without losing their relationship.
options.viewport: A compact package packet opens stepwise into portrait proofs and allowance detail as the user advances.
options.case: Excellent responsive behavior, but fold geometry adds interpretation cost to familiar controls.
options.kept: Compact summaries deploy detail progressively while preserving the complete state graph.
options.risk: Diagonal seams would fight portrait crops and reduce tap-target clarity.

options.label: The Instruction Weather
options.thesis: Plain-language actions physically transform into package state, turning instructions into visible consequences.
options.viewport: Generate condenses into eight candidate labels, then settles into a stable proof strip beneath the selected portrait.
options.case: Expressive state motion, but language-as-weather competes with faces and harms task predictability.
options.kept: Status motion must be deterministic, reversible, and readable throughout transformation.
options.risk: The signature interaction would dominate the product instead of serving package fulfillment.

canonCard.label: The category standard
canonCard.thesis: A polished SaaS wizard with a stepper, upload card, candidate grid, settings cards, and sticky primary button.
canonCard.viewport: A conventional top stepper leads into one white task card, with package status in a sidebar and the primary action at the bottom.
canonCard.risk: Immediately usable, but visually interchangeable with unrelated AI tools and likely to repeat the current hierarchy problem.
